**UPDATE 2026-05-30 — root cause CONFIRMED at last: a cracked brass Y-splitter at the far spigot**, not the hose and not the pressure regulator. Replacing the splitter restored full pressure at the far bed. This is the current truth; everything below is the chase that got here.

**CORRECTION to my 2026-04-02 diagnosis (I got this WRONG):** I first modeled the low pressure as a kinked hose and coiled it differently — no change. Then I blamed the regulator and swapped it — still no change. The regulator swap was a **red herring**; pressure at the near spigot was always fine, which should have pointed at the splitter sooner.

**Dead-ends — do NOT re-try:**
- Re-coiling / replacing the hose — the hose was never the problem.
- Swapping the pressure regulator — proven irrelevant (near spigot fine both times).
- Cleaning the aerator screen — cosmetic, no pressure effect.

**How to apply:** if far-bed pressure drops again, check the Y-splitter FIRST. See [[sprinkler-timer]] — same brass-fitting failure mode showed up there.
